story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, and the Flyers are winless in three (0-2-1). This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Flyers last (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth (tied for 16th).

The Rangers (32nd) and the Flyers (30th) both get a lot of their shots blocked. The Flyers pick their shots (3rd lowest). Philadelphia has scored 1.93 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Rangers get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (3rd lowest). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 9 A / 13 P in 15 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, with nine points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against the Rangers. Matvei Michkov (9 G / 2 A / 11 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL.

Dylan Garand (4-5-1 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for the Rangers. Philadelphia has two options in net: Joseph Woll (1-5-2 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) and Dan Vladař (2-3-2 / .888 SV% in 7 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Woll got the last one on Oct 28. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
